title: Unit 3 : Session 1 : SLO 1 — State and Prove De Morgan's Theorems
sections: 1. State De Morgan's Theorems (Remember)
The complement of the sum of two variables is equal to the PRODUCT of the COMPLEMENTS of the variables. (A + B)' = A' . B'
The complement of the product of two variables is equal to the SUM of the COMPLEMENTS of the variables. (A . B)' = A' + B'
2. Match the Expressions (Understand)
1. (X + Y)' → d. The complement of a sum
2. X' . Y' → c. The product of the complements
3. (X . Y)' → b. The complement of a product
4. X' + Y' → a. The sum of the complements
3. Complete the Proof (Apply) — Truth table for (A + B)' = A' . B'
Since the columns for (A + B)' and A' . B' are identical in every row, the theorem is proved.
4. Simplify the Expression (Analyze)
Step 1: F = ((A . B)')' . C'   (De Morgan's theorem applied to the outer complement)
Step 2: F = (A . B) . C'       (law of double complementation)
Final simplified expression: F = A . B . C'
5. Construct a Proof (Create) — Truth table for (A . B)' = A' + B'
The columns for (A . B)' and A' + B' are identical, so the second theorem is proved.
